name: IEC NOR gate (rectangular form)
summary: IEC ≥1 element with a negated output; the output is active only when none of the inputs are active.
description: The IEC NOR element is drawn as the ≥1 OR box with a negation circle at the output. Its output is at the external 1 state only when every input is inactive, which makes it a natural way to show an all-healthy or all-clear permissive on a logic sheet.

Interlock diagrams sometimes use the NOR element to produce a ready signal from a list of blocking conditions. The reader should check whether the blocking inputs are themselves negated, because a double negation can turn the function back into an AND of healthy signals.

As with all combinative IEC elements, the drawing says nothing about the response time or the electrical output stage. A NOR used in a safety function must also be traced to its implementing device to confirm the safety rating.
readingNotes: Count negations along the path; NOR with negated inputs is an AND of the uncomplemented signals.
Confirm which external level corresponds to the active state.
drawingChecklist: Place the negation mark at the output edge.
Reference the implementing hardware or program block.
distinction: A ≥1 element without the output circle is a plain OR; the circle is the only difference.
